entry.name: BVT-20
entry.title: BiView-Touch: Learning Bimanual Tactile Representations by Cross-Hand Completion
entry.summary: 44.2 h of bimanual tactile recordings from 22 right-handed participants over 20 coordination tasks (peg insertion, three-pin plug insertion, nut and bolt, block transfer, buckle and others), 6,893 sessions, each task recorded in paired active and support roles with the hands swapped, with whole-hand touch on both hands and MANUS hand tracking.
entry.hand: tactile gloves on both hands (make not stated)

sensor.note: The method uses 290 taxels per hand in a mirrored canonical order, grouped into 11 anatomical regions; the paper does not tie this count to BVT-20 explicitly.

entry.access: The paper says 'We collect and release BVT-20' and points to an anonymous 4open.science project page, which returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-23; no download link found.
caveats: Glove make, sensor type, coverage and sampling rate are not given in the paper; 'acquisition details' are deferred to the project website, which was not reachable.
Wrist-motion labels were derived from MANUS skeletal tracking; whether video was recorded is not stated.
Task T17 (buckle) is held out in the paper for transfer evaluation.

tracking.note: skeletal tracking used to derive wrist-motion labels

sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.23352 (datasets, BVT-20 statistics, task table, release sentence)
unconfirmed: taxels_per_hand 290 is the method's canonical layout; it is assumed to be BVT-20's layout because BVT-20 is used for transfer without a stated remapping.
MANUS tracking method set to 'magnetic' because MANUS gloves track by EMF; the paper names only 'MANUS skeletal tracking'.
Availability 'announced': the paper calls the dataset released, but no download was reachable.
